## Household and background

Zuri Bennett (born September 12, 1985 — 40) is single with no dependents and rents at 44 Foxglove Terrace in Anytown. She supervises the vet techs at Silver Birch Veterinary Clinic: one W-2, box 1 wages $47,614.00, box 2 federal withholding $5,610.00. The clinic's current health plan is a low-deductible PPO — she has not been HSA-eligible since 2023 — but the HSA she funded in her HDHP years is still open at Blue Spruce Health Savings Trust.

This year she drew $6,840.00 out of that HSA (Form 1099-SA box 1, code 1). Her receipts support $4,395.00 of qualified medical expenses — a dental crown ($1,890.00), physical-therapy copays ($1,105.00), and prescriptions ($1,400.00). The remaining $2,445.00 covered a transmission repair, which she knows is not a medical expense.

## Interview

**Q.** How much of the $6,840 went to qualified medical expenses — do the receipts cover it?

**A.** $4,395 exactly — I kept every receipt. The other $2,445 paid for my car's transmission; I knew it would be taxable.

**Q.** Did you roll any of the distribution into another HSA within 60 days?

**A.** No — nothing went back in.

**Q.** Did you contribute anything to the HSA this year, or were you covered by a high-deductible plan at any point?

**A.** No on both — the clinic's PPO isn't HSA-eligible, so the account just sits and gets spent down.

**Q.** Are you 65 or older, or permanently and totally disabled? (Either would waive the 20% additional tax.)

**A.** No — I'm 40 and healthy; the car was the only thing that broke.

**Q.** Any dependents? Could anyone claim you as a dependent? Are you blind or a student? A U.S. citizen all year?

**A.** No to all of those, and yes — citizen all year.
